skill.name: test-build-error
skill.description: Tests error visibility for build step failures
skill.summary: Tests error visibility for build step failures
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns, no risk factors, and no static findings requiring verdicts. Context review of SKILL.md found a test fixture for build failure visibility, with no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe user instructions.

content.value_statement: Build systems often hide dependency failures or surface them without useful context. This skill provides a small failing fixture for checking how Claude, Codex, and Claude Code expose build step errors.
actual_capabilities: Defines a minimal skill named test-build-error.
Uses a Node 20 Alpine base image for build testing.
Runs a build step that attempts to install a nonexistent npm package.
Provides a simple command that would echo a success message after build completion.
Documents that the purpose is testing build step error visibility.
limitations: It is a test fixture, not an end-user automation skill.
The build step is intended to fail because the package name is nonexistent.
It does not diagnose or repair build failures automatically.
It does not provide runtime application behavior beyond a simple echo command.

use_cases.title: Validate Marketplace Build Logs
use_cases.description: Check whether a skill marketplace clearly displays failed dependency installation output.

use_cases.title: Test CI Failure Reporting
use_cases.description: Use a predictable build failure to verify that CI jobs preserve useful error details.

use_cases.title: Confirm Agent Installation Feedback
use_cases.description: Observe how Claude, Codex, or Claude Code reports a failed skill build during installation.

prompt_templates.title: Run The Fixture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check of build failure visibility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Install this skill and report the exact build error shown by the installer.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Build Logs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison across local and CI environments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the skill build locally and in CI, then summarize differences in the failure output.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Error Clarity
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether the build failure output identifies the missing package, failing step, and recovery path.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Failure Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this fixture as a baseline and propose a checklist for testing skill build error reporting.

output_examples.input: Install the fixture and summarize what failed.
output_examples.output: The build failed during dependency installation because the referenced package could not be found. The installer should show the failing build step and package name.

output_examples.input: Assess whether the error message is useful for a developer.
output_examples.output: A useful report names the dependency step, includes the package resolution failure, and distinguishes build failure from runtime failure.

output_examples.input: Explain what this skill is best used for.
output_examples.output: This skill is best used as a controlled failure case for validating build logs, installer feedback, and CI error visibility.

best_practices: Use this fixture only in test environments where a failed build is expected.
Record the full installer output so missing build details are easy to compare.
Pair this fixture with a passing skill to confirm both success and failure paths.
anti_patterns: Do not publish it as a functional user-facing productivity skill.
Do not treat the failed build as an unexpected runtime defect.
Do not use it to validate production dependency availability.

faq.question: What does this skill test?
faq.answer: It tests whether build step failures are visible when a skill fails during installation or packaging.

faq.question: Is the build expected to fail?
faq.answer: Yes. The build step references a nonexistent npm package, so failure is the intended behavior.

faq.question: Does it run application logic?
faq.answer: No. It is a minimal fixture for build diagnostics, not an application workflow.

faq.question: Which tools can use the report context?
faq.answer: The marketplace record lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tool targets.

faq.question: Can it help debug real projects?
faq.answer: It can help validate error reporting systems, but it does not analyze arbitrary project builds.

faq.question: Are there security findings?
faq.answer: No evidence of prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or dangerous instructions was found in the reviewed skill file.
